question.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Multiplicative Property
question.problem: Which of the following gives the value of the double integral ${∬}_{R}\frac{\sqrt{xy}\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}A$ over the rectangle $R=[1,2]\times [0,\pi ]?$
question.worked_solution:
We apply the multiplicative property of double integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{\sqrt{xy}\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}\frac{1}{x}\,{x}^{1/2}\,{y}^{1/2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}})\text{ }(\sqrt{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =({\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y)\end{aligned}
$$

judgment.reasoning: All 16 intended selections are supported by their own captured worked solutions. No submitted answers or grades were supplied. q-129549: integrating first in x gives 1/y-1/(y+1), whose integral is ln(4/3). q-72050: the separated factors are 60 and 1/3, giving 20. q-72266: 9(16/3)(2/3)=32. q-129568: successive integration gives [cos(y)-cos(y+π/4)] from 0 to π, equal to √2-2. q-129644: the inner integral is x+7/3; the odd term integrates to zero, leaving 14/3. q-164350 and q-164416: projection onto the xy-plane preserves the respective hyperbola equations, with centers (-1,4) and (0,-1). q-164401: setting y=0 gives (x-4)^2=4, hence the two lines x=2 and x=6 with arbitrary z. q-164412: y+3=(x+2)^2/2 has vertex (-2,-3). q-164477: x²+y²=2 with unrestricted z is a circular cylinder, a special elliptic cylinder. q-164479: a hyperbola extended along z is a hyperbolic cylinder. q-164510: x=y²/2+z²/4 is an elliptic paraboloid opening along positive x. The solution's phrase 'centered at O' informally denotes its vertex; a paraboloid has no center of central symmetry. q-164547: y²=2z extended along x is a parabolic cylinder. q-164554: completing squares gives y-2=2(x-1)²-4(z+2)², a hyperbolic paraboloid with saddle point (1,2,-2). MA's classification and intended option 4 are correct, but its statement that this surface is 'centered' there is mathematically inaccurate: a hyperbolic paraboloid has no center of central symmetry. The corrected description is preserved separately from MA's wording. q-164550: x²/16-(y+1)²/16+(z-2)²/8=1 has two positive squared terms and one negative, so it is a hyperboloid of one sheet centered at (0,-1,2). q-129941: on the given rectangle, the integrand factors as x^(-1/2)√y cos(y), yielding the stated product of single integrals.
